plans.buy_case: QCOM is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI 38.1 (oversold), price hugging lower Bollinger Band, BB squeeze active, and MACD inflecting upward—all occurring above the 200MA with golden cross intact. For a swing trader, this is a high-probability entry zone in a quality semiconductor leader with strong IP moats, though macro/regulatory headwinds prevent a higher conviction call.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 30-32 (your optimal buy zone) OR price to touch the lower Bollinger Band ($169.50–$170.00). Do not chase; this is mean-reversion, so patience on entry is critical. Confirm with MACD histogram remaining above zero.
plans.exit_condition: Take profits at 180–182 (upper BB / resistance), or exit immediately if RSI crosses above 70 (overbought exit). Hard stop: if price closes below 200MA (167.78) or RSI re-enters 20 zone without breaking 50MA support.
plans.risk: Semiconductor sector macro sensitivity (recession fears, China trade tensions, inventory cycles); neutral fundamentals mean catalyst-driven downside is possible. QCOM also trades heavy on earnings—avoid holding through earnings surprises.

plans.buy_case: FSLR is printing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI 34.4 in oversold territory, price pinned to lower Bollinger Band, and MACD histogram reversing off the valley—classic swing fuel. Golden cross (50MA > 200MA) confirms uptrend structure is intact, and renewable energy tailwinds remain a fundamental tailwind despite limited recent catalysts.
plans.entry_condition: Enter on RSI touching 30 or lower, OR on first daily close above the lower Bollinger Band with volume confirmation. Do not chase above $215.
plans.exit_condition: Take profits at 200MA resistance (~$235) or if RSI breaks above 70 without a new high. Hard stop below $203 (break of current support). Exit early if negative renewable energy policy news breaks.

plans.notes: This is a clean technical setup with reasonable risk/reward (~$26 upside vs. $8 downside = 3.25:1), but conviction is capped by thin fundamental recent data. Good trade for your profile if you can monitor position weekly. Size it 1–1.5 shares only given portfolio size (~$210–316 deployed, ~6–9% of capital).

plans.buy_case: CDNS is firing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI 28.6 in oversold territory, price pinned to the lower Bollinger Band with a squeeze active, and volume confirmation on the move down. The 200MA filter is satisfied (price above it), and the golden cross provides longer-term directional tailwind for a quality semiconductor infrastructure play.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 25 or lower, OR price to touch the lower Bollinger Band ($325–327 range). Do NOT chase at current levels. A second test of the BB low with higher volume would be ideal confirmation before committing capital.
plans.exit_condition: Take profits at RSI 65–70 (mean reversion target) or if price breaks above the 50MA convincingly (~$375). Hard stop: close if RSI falls below 20 AND price breaks below the 200MA—signals momentum failure and invalidates the setup.
plans.timeframe: 3–6 weeks (classic swing trade into potential relief rally)
plans.risk: Semiconductor sector volatility and macro headwinds could extend the downtrend before reversal. The news mentions 'potential near-term volatility,' which is honest but vague—monitor earnings/guidance risk. With only $3,694 in the portfolio, a full position could be 1–2 shares; size appropriately to limit drawdown to 2–3% maximum.
plans.note_for_student: This is a *patient* entry setup, not an urgent buy. You have the technical signals but not the absolute confirmation yet. A busy MIT schedule means you should wait for a cleaner entry rather than chase. CDNS is high-quality and won't disappear—let mean reversion do the work by waiting for RSI <25. If it never comes, the setup fails and you move on. Discipline > FOMO.

Golden cross + price above 200MA confirms uptrend structure is intact. Utilities are defensive plays ideal for neutral VIX environment.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 30-32 range (your buy zone) OR price to touch lower Bollinger Band ($72.50-$73.00). Don't chase at current RSI 43.8—patience for better entry will improve your R:R. Only buy if BB width stays compressed (squeeze breakout coming).

plans.buy_case: COHR is flashing a textbook mean-reversion setup: RSI 33.3 in oversold territory, price hugging the lower Bollinger Band (0.11 pct), and MACD histogram turning up from a valley—all with the price safely above the 200MA and a golden cross in place. The technical confluence is clean for a swing entry, but the lack of recent fundamental data (earnings, cash flow, backlog) is a material gap that prevents a high-conviction call.
plans.entry_condition: Wait for RSI to dip to 25–28 range OR price to touch the lower Bollinger Band itself (≈$269–271). Confirm MACD histogram crosses above zero on the daily. Do not chase; patience is cheaper than FOMO.
plans.exit_condition: Take 50% off at RSI 65–70 (overbought), trailing stop at 3% below recent swing high. Hard exit if price breaks below 200MA (246.86) on a close—that breaks the trend filter.
plans.risk: Sector rotation risk (tech weakness), missing fundamental deterioration (order backlog, margins, cash burn), and whipsaw if COHR fails to hold above 200MA. At $277, you'd deploy ~$1,850–$2,000 of your ~$3,694 portfolio (50–54%), which is reasonable but leaves little dry powder if a better setup emerges.
plans.additional_notes: Before committing: Pull the latest 10-Q, check for recent analyst downgrades, and scan insider trading. COHR is semiconductor/photonics-adjacent—check if the sector is in a drawdown vs. a bounce. If fundamentals are solid and the technicals dip to your entry zone, this is a clean 10–13% swing candidate with defined risk.
